title: Matthew Chapter 6 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Matthew chapter 6 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Matthew Chapter 6 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Matthew Chapter 6.

questions.question: In Matthew 6, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Take heed that ye do not your alms before men
But when thou doest alms, let not thy left hand know
And when thou prayest, thou shalt not be as the hypocrites
After this manner therefore pray ye
questions.correctAnswer: Take heed that ye do not your alms before men
questions.explanation: This is the first instruction given in the chapter about almsgiving.

questions.question: What should you not do when you give your alms, according to Matthew 6?
options: Tell everyone about your good deeds
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:2 states that you should not sound a trumpet before you like the hypocrites do.

questions.question: What should not know what the other is doing when you give alms?
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:3 instructs that when you do alms, your left hand should not know what your right hand does.

questions.question: Where should your alms be given, according to Matthew 6?
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:4 emphasizes that alms should be given in secret.

questions.question: How do hypocrites pray, as mentioned in Matthew 6?
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:5 describes hypocrites as loving to pray standing in the synagogues.

questions.question: What should you do when you pray, according to Matthew 6?
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:6 instructs to enter into your closet when you pray.

questions.question: What do the heathen think will help them be heard when they pray?
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:7 states that the heathen think they will be heard for their much speaking, referring to vain repetitions.

questions.question: What does your Father know before you ask Him?
options: What things ye have need of
questions.correctAnswer: What things ye have need of
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:8 tells us that your Father knows what things you have need of before you ask Him.

questions.question: How does Matthew 6:9 address God?
options: Our Father which art in heaven
questions.correctAnswer: Our Father which art in heaven
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:9 begins the Lord's Prayer with the address 'Our Father which art in heaven'.

questions.question: What should be done according to Matthew 6:10?
options: Thy will be done in earth
questions.correctAnswer: Thy will be done in earth
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:10 states 'Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven'.

questions.question: What is requested in Matthew 6:11?
options: Give us this day our daily bread
questions.correctAnswer: Give us this day our daily bread
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:11 contains the request 'Give us this day our daily bread'.

questions.question: True or False: The Father rewards openly those who pray in secret.
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:6 indicates that the Father which seeth in secret shall reward thee openly.

questions.question: True or False: Hypocrites give their alms in secret.
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:2 describes hypocrites as doing their alms to be seen of men, not in secret.

questions.question: True or False: The Lord’s Prayer begins with 'Hallowed be thy name'.
questions.explanation: The Lord's Prayer begins with 'Our Father which art in heaven', as stated in Matthew 6:9.

questions.question: True or False: We are instructed to ask for forgiveness for our neighbors' debts.
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:12 states we should ask for forgiveness for our debts, as we forgive our debtors, not our neighbors' debts specifically.

medium.title: Matthew Chapter 6 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Matthew Chapter 6 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What should you not do when you fast, according to Matthew 6:16?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Matthew 6:16 states, 'Moreover when ye fast, be not, as the hypocrites, of a sad countenance...'

questions.question: What does Matthew 6:14 promise will happen if you forgive men their trespasses?
options: Your heavenly Father will forgive you
You will be rewarded by men
questions.correctAnswer: Your heavenly Father will forgive you
questions.explanation: This is supported by Matthew 6:14 which says, 'For if ye forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.'

questions.question: According to Matthew 6:18, where should you appear when you fast?
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:18 indicates, 'That thou appear not unto men to fast, but unto thy Father which is in secret...'

questions.question: What does Matthew 6:20 instruct you to do with treasures?
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:20 states, 'But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven...'

questions.question: What is said about the eye in Matthew 6:22?
options: It is the window to the soul
It must be single for the body to be full of light
It is the most important organ
questions.correctAnswer: It must be single for the body to be full of light
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:22 says, 'The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light.'

questions.question: According to Matthew 6:21, what does your treasure indicate?
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:21 states, 'For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.'

questions.question: In Matthew 6:24, what is stated about serving two masters?
options: You will eventually love one and hate the other
questions.correctAnswer: You will eventually love one and hate the other
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:24 says, 'No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other...'

questions.question: What should you do when you pray, according to Matthew 6:6?
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:6 instructs, 'But thou, when thou prayest, enter into thy closet...'

questions.question: What does Matthew 6:15 warn about forgiveness?
options: You will be forgiven if you forgive
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:15 states, 'But if ye forgive not men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.'

questions.question: What does Matthew 6:19 say about earthly treasures?
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:19 warns, 'Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt...'

questions.question: What is the main focus of Matthew 6:7 regarding prayer?
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:7 cautions, 'But when ye pray, use not vain repetitions, as the heathen do...'

questions.question: According to Matthew 6:5, how should you not pray?
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:5 states, 'And when thou prayest, thou shalt not be as the hypocrites are...'

questions.question: Is it true that your Father knows what you need before you ask Him?
questions.explanation: This is true as stated in Matthew 6:8, 'for your Father knoweth what things ye have need of, before ye ask him.'

questions.question: Is it false that you should showcase your fasting to others?
questions.explanation: This is false as Matthew 6:16 clearly advises against appearing sad like hypocrites when fasting.

questions.question: Is it false that where your treasure is, your heart will also be?
questions.explanation: This is false because Matthew 6:21 states, 'For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.'

hard.title: Matthew Chapter 6 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Matthew Chapter 6.

questions.question: According to Matthew 6:25, what should we not take thought for?
options: What ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink; nor yet for your body, what ye shall put on
What ye shall say when ye are accused
questions.correctAnswer: What ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink; nor yet for your body, what ye shall put on
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:25 explicitly instructs to take no thought for life, what to eat or drink, nor for the body what to put on.

questions.question: In Matthew 6:26, what example does Jesus use to illustrate God's provision?
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:26 uses the fowls of the air as an example, noting they do not sow or reap but are fed by the heavenly Father.

questions.question: What question does Jesus pose in Matthew 6:27 about anxiety's effect on life?
options: Which of you by taking thought can add one cubit unto his stature?
Who among you can extend his lifespan by worrying?
Can you double your wealth by anxious thinking?
Will God hear your prayers if you fret?
questions.correctAnswer: Which of you by taking thought can add one cubit unto his stature?
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:27 asks rhetorically if anyone can add a cubit to their height by worrying, illustrating anxiety's futility.

questions.question: In Matthew 6:28-29, what comparison is made to show God's provision in clothing?
options: The lilies of the field are more gloriously clothed than Solomon in all his glory
The cedar trees are more majestic than the temple's gold
The sparrows are more cared for than the rich
The stars are more numerous than the grains of sand
questions.correctAnswer: The lilies of the field are more gloriously clothed than Solomon in all his glory
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:28-29 compares lilies, which toil not yet are arrayed more gloriously than Solomon, to demonstrate God's care.

questions.question: According to Matthew 6:30, what reason is given to trust God's provision?
options: If God so clothes the grass of the field, he will much more clothe you
If you fast, God will reward you openly
If you give alms secretly, God will reward you openly
If you pray in public, men will reward you
questions.correctAnswer: If God so clothes the grass of the field, he will much more clothe you
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:30 states God clothes the grass of the field, which is temporary, so He will much more clothe those of little faith.

questions.question: What priority does Matthew 6:33 instruct believers to have?
options: Seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: Seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:33 commands seeking first God's kingdom and righteousness, promising all other needs will be added.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'noieo' (νοέω) in Matthew 6:27 mean?
questions.explanation: 'Noieo' in Matthew 6:27 means 'to think' or 'to consider,' referring to the act of anxious thought about one's stature.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Matthew 6:25-34 to teach about reliance on God?
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:25-34 uses parallelism, repeating similar structures about not worrying about life, food, and clothing to reinforce trust in God.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of God's provision found in Matthew 6:25-34?
questions.explanation: Psalm 23:1-4 echoes God's provision and care for His people, paralleling Matthew 6:25-34's theme of trusting God's sustenance.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage connects to the teaching on treasures in heaven in Matthew 6:19-21?
questions.explanation: Luke 12:33-34 parallels Matthew 6:19-21 by teaching about laying up treasures in heaven and where the heart will be also.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Matthew 6:25 in the chapter?
options: No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other
Be not ye therefore like unto them
When thou prayest, enter into thy closet
Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth
questions.correctAnswer: No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:24 immediately precedes 6:25, stating no man can serve two masters, setting the context for trust in God rather than mammon.

questions.question: How does Matthew 6:6's instruction about secret prayer contrast with Matthew 6:5's description of hypocrites?
options: Private prayer is rewarded openly, while public prayer for show receives only human reward
Public prayer is more effective than private prayer
Prayer must always be loud and repeated
Giving alms publicly is better than secretly
questions.correctAnswer: Private prayer is rewarded openly, while public prayer for show receives only human reward
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:5-6 contrasts hypocritical public prayer with secret prayer, highlighting God's reward for sincerity versus human praise.

questions.question: What typological significance can be seen in the lilies of the field mentioned in Matthew 6:28-29?
options: They symbolize God's provision and beauty beyond human effort
They foreshadow the resurrection of Jesus
They illustrate the law of Moses
questions.correctAnswer: They symbolize God's provision and beauty beyond human effort
questions.explanation: The lilies in Matthew 6:28-29 typify God’s providential care and glory that surpasses human labor or Solomon’s wealth.

questions.question: Which Greek word in Matthew 6:33 translated as 'seek' implies a diligent, purposeful search?
questions.explanation: 'Zēteō' in Matthew 6:33 means to seek or strive after something with intent, emphasizing earnest pursuit of God's kingdom.

questions.question: True or False: Matthew 6:34 instructs believers to worry about tomorrow because it will take care of itself.
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:34 instructs to take no thought for tomorrow, as each day has enough trouble of its own, discouraging worry.

theological.title: Matthew Chapter 6 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Matthew Chapter 6 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Matthew 6:4 teach about God's nature in relation to secret acts of righteousness?
options: God rewards openly what is done in secret
God is indifferent to secret acts
questions.correctAnswer: God rewards openly what is done in secret
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:4 states, "thy Father which seeth in secret himself shall reward thee openly," teaching that God sees secret acts and rewards them openly, demonstrating His just and omniscient nature.

questions.question: What doctrine about human sin does Matthew 6:15 teach regarding forgiveness?
options: God forgives regardless of human response
Sin is automatically forgiven by God
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:15 says, "if ye forgive not men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses," showing the doctrine that unforgiveness hinders receiving God's forgiveness.

questions.question: What doctrine does Matthew 6:33 teach about the priority of the kingdom of God in salvation?
options: Seeking God's kingdom and righteousness is primary and leads to provision
Material needs must be sought first
Righteousness is unrelated to God's kingdom
The kingdom of God is delayed until after provision is secured
questions.correctAnswer: Seeking God's kingdom and righteousness is primary and leads to provision
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:33 instructs, "But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you," teaching the prioritization of God’s kingdom and righteousness in the life of the believer.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Matthew 6:8 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:8 says, "your Father knoweth what things ye have need of, before ye ask him," demonstrating God's omniscience, His complete knowledge of our needs.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is illustrated in Matthew 6:26 regarding God's care for creation?
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:26 shows God's providence as He cares for the birds of the air, indicating His ongoing provision and care for His creation.

questions.question: How does Matthew 6:19-21 connect to the broader biblical theme of eternal treasure vs. earthly impermanence?
options: It contrasts earthly decay with heavenly permanence
It promotes earthly wealth as ultimate
It denies any value in heavenly treasure
It encourages accumulation of treasures on earth
questions.correctAnswer: It contrasts earthly decay with heavenly permanence
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:19-21 teaches storing treasure in heaven rather than on earth, connecting to the biblical theme (e.g., 1 Timothy 6:17-19) of eternal, imperishable rewards versus temporary earthly wealth.

questions.question: In what way does Matthew 6:5-6 prepare for the New Testament emphasis on personal and private prayer?
options: By teaching that prayer should be sincere and not for show
By commanding public displays of prayer
questions.correctAnswer: By teaching that prayer should be sincere and not for show
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:5-6 contrasts hypocritical public prayers with private prayer to the Father in secret, preparing for the New Testament emphasis on heartfelt, sincere communication with God.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Matthew 6:14 and Matthew 6:15 teach about forgiveness and God's response?
options: Human forgiveness is necessary to receive divine forgiveness
Divine forgiveness is unconditional irrespective of human action
Forgiveness is irrelevant to the believer’s relationship with God
God forgives only sins committed publicly
questions.correctAnswer: Human forgiveness is necessary to receive divine forgiveness
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:14-15 teach that forgiving others is a prerequisite for receiving forgiveness from God, establishing a reciprocal dynamic in the doctrine of forgiveness.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Matthew 6:22-23 teach about spiritual perception and moral influence?
options: The eye as the lamp of the body symbolizes spiritual focus affecting moral condition
Darkness and light are unrelated to morality
Only external actions matter for the heart
questions.correctAnswer: The eye as the lamp of the body symbolizes spiritual focus affecting moral condition
questions.explanation: Verses 22-23 use metaphor of the eye’s condition affecting the whole body’s light or darkness, teaching that spiritual perception influences moral and spiritual health.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about worry and faith in God's provision is taught in Matthew 6:25 and 6:33?
options: Trust in God's provision should replace anxious worry
God does not care for physical needs
Faith and worry can coexist without conflict
questions.correctAnswer: Trust in God's provision should replace anxious worry
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:25 commands not to worry about life’s necessities, and 6:33 calls for seeking God's kingdom first, promising provision, teaching trust in divine care over anxiety.

questions.question: Skeptics claim that Matthew 6:7-8 teaches that prayers are ineffective without many words. What does Matthew 6:7-8 actually teach?
options: Prayers should be sincere and not vain repetitions because God already knows our needs
Prayers must be lengthy to be heard
God only hears prayers with many words
Repetitive prayer is a way to earn God's favor
questions.correctAnswer: Prayers should be sincere and not vain repetitions because God already knows our needs
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:7-8 warns against vain repetitions and teaches that God knows our needs before we ask, emphasizing sincere, meaningful prayer over verbosity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Matthew 6:24 teach about loyalty and the incompatibility of serving God and mammon?
options: One cannot serve two masters; loyalty must be exclusive to God
It is possible to serve both God and wealth equally
Mammon is not a real master
Serving God requires serving mammon first
questions.correctAnswer: One cannot serve two masters; loyalty must be exclusive to God
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:24 teaches the exclusivity of loyalty in service, that a person cannot serve both God and mammon, emphasizing the doctrine of undivided allegiance to God.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated in Matthew 6:30 regarding God's care for believers?
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:30 illustrates God’s faithful care in clothing and providing for His creation, encouraging trust despite human little faith.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Matthew 6:16 and 6:18 teach about fasting and sanctification?
options: True fasting is done in secret and God rewards it openly
Fasting is only about public display
God rewards only fasting with sad countenance
questions.correctAnswer: True fasting is done in secret and God rewards it openly
questions.explanation: Verses 16 and 18 contrast hypocritical public fasting with secret fasting before God, teaching that sanctification involves sincere, private devotion rewarded by God.

questions.question: How does Matthew 6:13, the conclusion of the Lord's Prayer, reflect the doxological affirmation of God's eternal sovereignty?
options: It declares God's kingdom, power, and glory forever
It emphasizes human power over God
It omits mention of God's glory
questions.correctAnswer: It declares God's kingdom, power, and glory forever
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:13 ends the Lord's Prayer with a doxology affirming God’s eternal kingdom, power, and glory, underscoring His sovereign authority.
